sources.title: What is an autopilot in Microsoft Foundry?
sources.dateEvidence: Page metadata records ms.date 2026-08-25 and updated_at 2026-08-26T22:14:00Z.

evidence.quote: Autopilot, previously called Scout, is your digital teammate.
Autopilot lives in your tenant with its own identity, memory, computer and workspace, and it’s built on Microsoft IQ so it understands how your organization actually works.
You set the objective and boundaries; Autopilot handles the rest while keeping you informed and in control.
Home and Code will start rolling out in our Frontier program in the coming weeks and Autopilot is expanding to private preview at the end of the month.

An autopilot is a type of agent that works under its own identity as a persistent, named member of your organization. It holds a standing role rather than answering one request at a time. It has its own security profile in your tenant and a manager who's responsible for it.
Capabilities describe an autopilot. Identity establishes it.

evidence.locator: What doesn't define an autopilot, autonomy paragraph
evidence.quote: An autopilot doesn't have to be fully autonomous: your organization controls when it responds, who it can interact with, what it can access, and which actions it can take.

evidence.locator: Why you build a blueprint, not an autopilot
evidence.quote: You don't build an autopilot. You build a blueprint that teams use to create their own autopilot instances, each with its own identity and its own team-scoped access.
What it never grants is access to a specific team's business resources.
Every instance created from the blueprint has its own identity, permissions, and assignment.

claims.wording: Copilot Autopilot, previously Scout, was announced as a persistent digital teammate with its own identity, memory, computer and workspace; people set objectives and boundaries and remain in control.
Microsoft said Copilot Autopilot was expanding to private preview at the end of September 2026; the announcement does not establish general availability.
As an architectural lens, Microsoft Foundry defines an autopilot by its standing role, identity, security profile and accountable manager, not by a changing feature list.
In the Foundry model, autonomy remains bounded: the organization controls when an autopilot responds, who it interacts with, what it accesses and which actions it can take.
The Foundry blueprint model separates reusable logic and infrastructure from team-specific access; each instance receives its own identity, permissions and assignment.

knownGaps: The public announcement does not provide general-availability timing for Copilot Autopilot.
The Foundry identity and blueprint model is used only as an architectural lens; the sources do not establish that every Copilot Autopilot implementation is identical.
No customer outcome, savings estimate or production operating metric was provided by the selected sources.
This project intentionally excludes Windows Autopilot device provisioning and private enterprise records.
